354011.title: Invertibility conjecture for a cyclotomic circulant matrix
354011.statement: Let $q=p^s$ be a prime power, let $Q=q^m$, and let $N$ be a divisor of $Q-1$. Write $N_1=(Q-1)/N$ and let $A$ be the circulant matrix defined in equation from the relevant Gaussian periods. **Invertibility conjecture.** The circulant matrix $A$ is invertible. This conjecture is motivated by numerical computations suggesting that the associated polynomial does not vanish at the relevant roots of unity; its validity would support the characterization of constant $b$-symbol weight irreducible cyclic codes and is noted as a question of interest in cyclotomy.

354060.title: Boundedness of cumulant correction terms for the three-letter pair count
354060.statement:
Let $T_r$ denote the correction to the $r$th cumulant of $X^{(n)}_3$ arising from dependence among the pair indicators. **Cumulant-correction conjecture.**

$$
|T_.|=\mathcal{O}(1).
$$

The surrounding argument explains that bounded corrections, in particular for the third and fourth cumulants, would suffice for the proposed Gaussian limiting distribution of $X^{(n)}_3$. The notation $T_. $ is schematic in the source, so the precise range of cumulant orders intended should be checked against the full paper.

354565.title: Translated V-strict promotion order conjecture
354565.statement:
Let $V=\{a,b,c\}$ be the three-element poset with $a\lessdot b$ and $a\lessdot c$, let $\mathcal{L}_{V\times[\ell]}(R^q)$ denote the set of $V$-strict labelings with restriction function $R^q$, and let $\operatorname*{Pro}$ denote promotion. **Translated V-strict promotion order conjecture.** Promotion on $\mathcal{L}_{V\times[\ell]}(R^q)$ has order dividing

$$
2q.
$$

This is presented as equivalent to the V-poset rowmotion conjecture; computational evidence and a reflection interpretation support it, but it remains unproved.

354891.title: Vanishing Einstein spectral functional for suitably regular spectral triples of dimension 2
354891.statement:
Let $({\mathcal A},D,{\mathcal H})$ be a suitably regular spectral triple of dimension $2$, and let the Einstein spectral functional be the functional introduced in the paper from this spectral triple.

**Vanishing Einstein functional conjecture.** The Einstein spectral functional vanishes.

This is proposed as a direction for further computation, motivated by the expectation that the spectral Einstein functional should vanish for more general spectral triples over noncommutative two-tori. The statement is presented as an expectation rather than established result.

354983.title: First-player conjecture for rectangular grid instances of INFLUENCE
354983.statement:
Let $G_{n,m}$ be the rectangular grid with $n$ rows and $m$ columns, with alternated black and white vertices and a black vertex in the top-left corner. Let $Ls(G_{n,m})$ and $Rs(G_{n,m})$ denote the left and right scores of the corresponding game. **Rectangular-grid first-player conjecture.** For $n,m\geq 2$,

$$
Ls(G_{n,m})>0>Rs(G_{n,m}).
$$

In particular, the first player wins and there is no draw.

Despite the symmetry of rectangular grids, there is no BW-automorphism, and the computations reported in the source all give a first-player victory; the conjecture remains unproved in general.

355040.title: Equality of nonnegative and zero-one tensor spectral-to-Frobenius ratios
355040.statement:
For a tensor dimension $n_1\times n_2\times\dots\times n_d$, let $\phi(\mathbb{R}^{n_1\times n_2\times\dots\times n_d}_+)$ be the infimum of the spectral-to-Frobenius norm ratio over nonnegative real tensors, and let $\phi(\mathbb{B}^{n_1\times n_2\times\dots\times n_d})$ be the corresponding quantity over zero-one tensors. **Ratio equality conjecture.**

$$
\phi(\mathbb{R}^{n_1\times n_2\times\dots\times n_d}_+)=\phi(\mathbb{B}^{n_1\times n_2\times\dots\times n_d}).
$$

The authors describe this as a bold conjecture motivated by exhaustive searches for small dimensions and believe the resulting upper bounds are tight; exact values for the other small dimensions were not established in the paper.

355106.title: The small sphere hypothesis implies the small gap property
355106.statement:
Let $G$ be a finitely generated, virtually nilpotent group with the Small Sphere (SS) Property. For $r\in(0,1)$, define the small gap property (SG property) by requiring that there is some $\delta>0$ such that

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\eta_n(G,\delta)>r,
$$

where

$$
\eta_n(G,\delta)=\min\{\rho(A,B):g_B(A)<\delta,\ A,B\text{ subballs of }G,\ |A|>n\}
$$

and

$$
\rho(A,B)=\left\{\frac{|C|}{|A|}:C\subseteq A\cap B\text{ is a subball}\right\}.
$$

**Small sphere to small gap conjecture.** Then $G$ has the SG property. The SG property would provide the ball-intersection control needed for the SBM theory; it is known for $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with standard generators, but the source reports no verified non-abelian examples and leaves the general implication open.

355331.title: Concavity conjecture for the fundamental ratio on triangle moduli space
355331.statement:
Let $\xi(D)=\lambda_2(D)/\lambda_1(D)$ be the fundamental ratio of the first two Dirichlet–Laplacian eigenvalues. Consider the moduli space of triangles after quotienting by the symmetries of the problem. **Concavity conjecture for the fundamental ratio.** The function $\xi$ is concave on this moduli space.

This claim is suggested by numerical and visual evidence from the paper's parameter-space computations; no proof or resolution is supplied.

355348.title: Growth conjecture for the number of orderings of congruence-class biases
355348.statement:
Let $\mathscr{O}(t)$ denote the number of possible orderings arising from the biases among congruence classes for $k$-indivisible partitions, and let $\varphi(t)$ be Euler's totient function. **Growth conjecture.** As $t\to\infty$, we have

$$
\frac{\mathscr{O}(t)}{\varphi(t)}=o(t)
$$

and

$$
\log t=o\left(\frac{\mathscr{O}(t)}{\varphi(t)}\right).
$$

Thus the normalized number of orderings is conjectured to grow sublinearly in $t$ and faster than logarithmically. The claim is motivated by numerical evidence and remains open.

355377.title: Higher-degree Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv equality for equal parameters
355377.statement:
Let $q$ be a positive integer and let $t$ be a parameter for which the generalized Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant $4\mathsf{EGZ}({t},{q},{q})4$ and the generalized Davenport constant $4\mathsf{D}_{({},{q})}({\mathbb{Z}_q})4$ are defined. **The conjecture.**

$$
\mathsf{EGZ}({t},{q},{q})=t+q^2-q=t+\mathsf{D}_{({},{q})}({\mathbb{Z}_q})-q.
$$

This conjecture is motivated by the preceding theorem and computational evidence; the supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or disproved.

355429.title: Explicit triangular limit shape for Young diagrams on the diamond
355429.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be the open diamond

$$
|x|+|y|<1/\sqrt2
$$

and let $\Phi$ be the limiting variational function for a homogeneous Poisson point process on $\Omega$; its derivative $\Phi'$ is the corresponding Young-diagram limit shape. **Triangular limit-shape formula.**

$$
\Phi'(r)=\begin{cases}\sqrt2-r & \text{if $0\le r\le\sqrt2$,}\\0 & \text{if $r>\sqrt2$.}\end{cases}
$$

This is the explicit formulation of the triangular shape suggested by computer simulations. It remains open in the source and, if proved, would provide the claimed explicit limit surfaces and a new derivation of the Logan–Shepp–Vershik–Kerov limit shape.

355525.title: Nonexistence of binary quasi group codes with involutory permutation automorphism group
355525.statement:
Let $C$ be a binary quasi group code of length $n=2m>2$, and let $\operatorname{PAut}(C)$ denote its permutation automorphism group. **Nonexistence conjecture.** There is no binary quasi group code $C$ of length $n=2m>2$ such that

$$
\operatorname{PAut}(C)\cong C_2.
$$

This conjecture generalizes the preceding nonexistence result for lengths $2<n=2m\leq 8$; the authors report that computer calculations suggest it, but a proof would require handling many cases.

355824.title: Periodicity conjecture for the Delta-triangle
355824.statement:
Let $p\geq2$ be an integer, and let $P=\Delta(p)$, where

$$
\Delta(p)=\{(i,k)\in[p]\times[p]\mid i+k>p+1\}.
$$

Let $f\in\mathbb{K}^{\widehat{P}}$ be a $\mathbb{K}$-labeling such that $R^pf\neq\operatorname{\bot}$. Set $a=f(0)$ and $b=f(1)$, and for $x\in\widehat{P}$ define $x'\in\widehat{P}$ by $x'=x$ when $x=0$ or $x=1$, and by $x'=(j,i)$ when $x=(i,j)$. **Periodicity conjecture for the Delta-triangle.** The elements $a$ and $b$ are invertible, and

$$
(R^pf)(x)=a\overline{b}\cdot f(x')\cdot\overline{a}b.
$$

This is suggested by computations for $p=3$ and would extend the commutative rectangular-poset periodicity theorem to these triangular posets; its resolution is not stated in the supplied text.

356015.title: Small-set isoperimetric conjecture for high-dimensional product graphs
356015.statement:
Let $G$ be a high-dimensional product graph whose base graphs are connected, regular, and of bounded size, and let $d$ be the degree of $G$. For a subset $X\subseteq V(G)$, write $e(X,X^c)$ for the number of edges between $X$ and its complement. **Small-set isoperimetric conjecture.** If

$$
\log |X| \ll d,
$$

then

$$
e(X,X^c)=(1-o(1))d|X|.
$$

This would provide a qualitatively stronger isoperimetric inequality for small sets in high-dimensional product graphs, analogous to the near-optimal expansion known for small sets in the hypercube. The source presents this as a belief that would yield a shorter proof of the supercritical percolation result, rather than as an established theorem.

356067.title: Conjecture on the limiting distribution of maximal persistence in random clique complexes
356067.statement:
Let $X(n,p)$ be the random clique complex, let $M_k(n)$ denote the maximal persistence over all $k$-dimensional cycles in $X(n,p)$), and let

$$
f_k(n)=n^{1/k(k+1)}(\log n)^{1/(k+1)}.
$$

**Limiting-distribution conjecture.** The random variable

$$
\frac{M_k(n)}{f_k(n)}
$$

converges in law to a limiting distribution supported on an interval $[\lambda_k,\infty)$ for some $\lambda_k>0$. Such a limit theorem would give precise probabilities for the existence of cycles whose persistence exceeds a specified threshold. The source offers this as a conjecture illustrated by numerical experiments and gives no resolution.

356253.title: Finite positivity conjecture for copartition generating functions
356253.statement:
Let $a,b,m,N,M\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $(x;q)_k$ denote the finite $q$-Pochhammer symbol. **Finite positivity conjecture.** If $b\mid a$ and $a+b=m$, then the $q$-series

$$
\frac{(-q^{m};q^m)_{N+M-1}}{(-q^a;q^m)_N(q^b;q^m)_M}
$$

has non-negative coefficients when $N\leq M$. This is a proposed finite analogue of the infinite-product positivity conjecture; the supplied text gives computational evidence but no proof or resolution.

356261.title: The smaller-game conjecture for correlated equilibrium polytopes
356261.statement:
Let $G$ be a $(2\times n)$-game with generic payoff matrices, and let $P_G$ be its correlated equilibrium polytope. A polytope is **full-dimensional** when it has maximal dimension in its ambient correlated equilibrium space.

**Smaller-game conjecture.** If $P_G$ is not of maximal dimension, then there exists a $(2\times k)$-game $G'$ with $k<n$ such that $P_{G'}$ has maximal dimension and $P_G$ and $P_{G'}$ are combinatorially equivalent.

For $(2\times 3)$-games, the preceding results establish the corresponding reduction to smaller games, and computations support the claim for $(2\times n)$-games with $n\leq 5$. The conjecture predicts that every non-maximal correlated equilibrium polytope in this family has the combinatorial type of a maximal polytope arising from a smaller game.

356606.title: Uniqueness-set conjecture for the extremal zero set
356606.statement:
Let $\varphi_p$ be the unique solution of the extremal problem, let $\mathscr{Z}(\varphi_p)$ denote its zero set, and let $PW^p$ be the Paley–Wiener space. A set is a **uniqueness set** for $PW^p$ if the only function in $PW^p$ vanishing on it is the zero function. **Uniqueness-set conjecture.**

$$
\mathscr{Z}(\varphi_p)\cup\{0\}\text{ is a uniqueness set for }PW^p\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p\geq1.
$$

The assertion has been verified in the source for $p\geq2$ and remains to be checked below $2$.

356828.title: NP-completeness of maximal independent queen domination on polyominoes
356828.statement:
A **polyomino** is a finite union of edge-connected unit squares in the plane. A set of queens is **independent** when no two queens attack each other, and it is **maximal dominating** when it dominates every square and no queen can be added while preserving independence.

**Maximal independent queen domination conjecture.** The maximal independent queen domination problem on polyominoes is NP-complete.

The conjecture asks whether the queen analogue of the known polynomial-time rook result becomes NP-complete already in dimension two. The paper reports extensive computations supporting this expectation, but no reduction is given.

381794.title: The simplicity conjecture for convex hulls of Wachs permutations
381794.statement:
Let $m\in\mathbb{P}$, and let $c(\operatorname{\mathcal{W}}(S_{2m}))$ be the convex hull of the Wachs permutations in $\mathbb{R}^{2m}$. **Simplicity conjecture.** The polytope $c(\operatorname{\mathcal{W}}(S_{2m}))$ is simple.

The authors verified this conjecture for $m\leqslant 5$, but report that SageMath shows $c(\operatorname{\mathcal{W}}(S_9))$ is not simple; this computational observation concerns the odd-dimensional analogue and does not resolve the stated even-index conjecture.
